value.title: Предупреждение об экономии памяти карты
value.surface: Foreground map warning and Map memory menu
value.meaning: Advisory render-resource economy status; slower tile/cache work does not authorize geometry thinning or data removal.
value.value_origin: RenderMemoryGuard -> MapFragment foreground/process claim or MainActivity menu -> showRenderMemoryStatus -> bounded message with fixed actions.
value.units: Resource state and optional layer names; not a measured free-memory quantity or render acknowledgment.
updates: Automatic display is claimed once per application process across maps and Activity recreation.
Manual menu display is independent of the automatic process claim.
actions: Reload calls the owning MapDrawable.retryMemoryLimitedLayers; its existing resource-policy re-evaluation remains unchanged.
conditions: Host must remain usable; automatic display additionally requires a resumed/visible map and resource notice.
The current guard restrictions() returns an empty map; the optional name list does not prove a particular layer lost geometry.
Programmatic dialog: no XML widgets. Complete title/actions reserve their measured height before the message scroll viewport.
value.saved_state: No new preference or persistent mode. RenderMemoryNotice owns an atomic static process-session claim.
expectations: Oracle: all129 technical polygon IDs and whole SQL row hashes remain complete through economy/recreation; one automatic notice, with manual access remaining available.

Oracle: each character has a layout line, no ellipsis, visible glyph extents fit, both complete actions remain inside the dialog and the message can scroll in narrow Russian portrait/landscape themes/font profiles.
Counterexample: clipping a button, thinning geometry, or treating this notice as an overdue-update timer.
unknowns: Extracted-helper native acceptance is pending. Earlier Full failed button bounds after correcting trailing-whitespace measurement.
Component profiles do not establish Full real-window, physical SM-X115, actual OOM/low-memory or all-map performance acceptance.
